hints: Strip away the story: you are looking for the longest contiguous stretch of trees that uses at most two different fruit types.
Use a sliding window with a count map of fruit types. When the map holds a third type, shrink from the left until only two types remain.

1. Keep a map count and left = 0.
  2. For each right, add trees[right] to the map.
  3. While the map has more than 2 keys, decrease the count of trees[left] (remove it at 0) and move left right.
  4. Update best with the window length.
  5. Return best.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: From every starting tree, walk right collecting types in a set until a third type appears.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Sliding window that keeps at most two distinct types, tracking the widest valid window.
approaches.space: O(1) (at most 3 keys in the map)

explain: For [3,3,1,3,2,2,1]: the window [3,3,1,3] has two types and length 4. Adding 2 makes three types, so the left end moves past 3, 3 and 1, leaving [3,2]; the next 2 makes it [3,2,2]. Adding 1 forces another shrink to [2,2,1]. The best seen is 4. Each tree enters and leaves the window at most once, so the scan is linear. Always remove a type from the map when its count reaches 0, otherwise the size check is wrong.
recognize: Longest contiguous stretch with at most K distinct values → sliding window with a frequency map.
